candidates.computation_change_reason: Each ceiling concentration establishes the enforceable numeric limit against which reported pollutant measurements would be compared; different interpretation of which pollutants or values apply would change exceedance determinations.

Whether limits are on a dry-weight basis affects how reported measurements must be normalized before comparison; a different basis interpretation would change whether a measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, or a reclamation site shall be treated by either the Class A or Class B pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a facility's land-application category falls within this set determines whether Class A or Class B pathogen limits and treatment standards apply, which changes both the numeric compliance thresholds and the monitoring/treatment obligations to be evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge that is applied to a lawn or home garden shall be treated by the Class A pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If a discharge or use is classified as lawn or home garden application, only Class A pathogen limits and associated demonstration requirements apply; misclassification would change applicable limits and required monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge that is sold or given away in a bag shall be treated by Class A pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Bagged sludge sold or given away triggers mandatory Class A treatment; interpretation of whether this condition applies changes which pathogen limits and compliance demonstrations govern the case.

candidates.locator: Page 3, Section part_i, §3.a Class A alternatives (introductory limits)
candidates.exact_span: All 6 options require either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge be less than 1000 Most Probable Number (MPN) per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of Salmonella sp. bacteria in the sewage sludge be less than three MPN per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis)
candidates.computation_change_reason: These are enforceable numeric pathogen limits and define which analytes must be monitored to demonstrate Class A compliance; different readings of the MPN thresholds or dry-weight basis would change exceedance results and monitoring scope.

candidates.locator: Page 3, Section part_i, §3.a Class A alternatives (timing)
candidates.exact_span: at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required sampling or demonstration timing determines which monitoring periods are obligated and whether absent results represent missing required evidence versus periods outside the compliance window.

candidates.locator: Page 3, Section part_i, §3.a Class A alternatives (Texas restriction)
candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 5 and 6 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class A sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If a permit relies on Alternative 5 or 6, this restriction would invalidate that compliance pathway and require evaluation under a different alternative with different numeric and monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: The pH of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be raised to above 12 and shall remain above 12 for 72 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 2 sets numeric pH and duration thresholds that must be met and presumably verified; interpretation of the pH level or 72-hour hold period changes compliance outcomes and what process monitoring is required.

candidates.exact_span: The temperature of the sewage sludge shall be above 52 degrees Celsius for 12 hours or longer during the period that the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Temperature and duration thresholds are operative compliance conditions; different interpretation of the 52°C or 12-hour requirement would change whether Alternative 2 is satisfied and what temperature monitoring is obligated.

candidates.exact_span: At the end of the 72 hour period during which the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12, the sewage sludge shall be air dried to achieve a percent solids in the sewage sludge greater than 50%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 50% solids threshold is a numeric compliance criterion tied to a specific process endpoint; interpretation affects whether the treatment demonstration passes and whether percent-solids monitoring was required.

candidates.exact_span: The pH shall be defined as the logarithm of the reciprocal of the hydrogen ion concentration measured at 25 degrees Celsius or measured at another temperature and then converted to an equivalent value at 25 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How pH is measured and temperature-corrected affects whether reported values satisfy the >12 requirement for Alternative 2 compliance.

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for enteric viruses prior to pathogen treatment. The limit for enteric viruses is one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric enteric-virus limit and a mandatory analysis obligation; interpretation of the 1 PFU/4 g limit or whether analysis may occur before versus after treatment changes compliance and monitoring applicability.

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for viable helminth ova prior
candidates.computation_change_reason: This truncated requirement indicates a helminth-ova analysis obligation under Alternative 3; whether this incomplete text is operative and what limit applies would affect whether monitoring was required and how missing helminth-ova evidence is classified.
